title: Metric—Phase Fields: Decoupling Distance and Sign for Thin-Structure Reconstruction from Unoriented Point Clouds
claim: Unsigned fields give noisy, unstable surfaces and signed fields inflate thin structures; our decoupled representation preserves thin geometry with a clean zero level set.
layout: 3 columns left-to-right, 3D renders over 2D slices, red zoom boxes
description: Three columns compare UDF, SDF and MPF (ours) on the same 3D plant-in-pot model. The top row shows the reconstructed surfaces. The UDF result is noisy and has holes. The SDF result is bloated, with thick, merged leaves. The MPF result is clean and has thin leaves and stems. A translucent plane cuts through each plant. A red box marks a region, and an inset zoom sits at the lower right of each model. The bottom row shows the 2D field slices along that plane, colored red to blue. The UDF slice has Voronoi-like cells. The SDF slice has large blue inside regions. The MPF slice has thin black zero-level contours. Large serif labels (UDF, SDF, MPF) sit beneath each column. The eye goes first to the 3D plants and the differences between them.
caption: Challenges of SDFs and UDFs in surface reconstruction. When the inside–outside sign is ambiguous (e.g., in thin plates, boundary regions, or non-manifold configurations), learning a single SDF becomes ill-conditioned and may introduce artifacts such as inflated thickness. In contrast, UDFs often suffer from optimization difficulties and unstable zero level set extraction due to non-differentiability at u = 0 and the lack of sign information. Black lines in the 2D slices indicate the zero-level set.
abstract: Neural Signed Distance Functions (SDFs) excel at reconstructing watertight manifolds but fail on thin structures and open boundaries due to strict inside--outside constraints. Conversely, Unsigned Distance Fields (UDFs) accommodate general geometries but suffer from gradient singularities at the zero-level set, hindering optimization and extraction. We introduce Metric--Phase Fields (MPFs), a decoupled implicit representation that separates metric proximity from topological phase. Given an unoriented point cloud, MPFs learn (i) an unsigned metric field $r$ and (ii) a smooth phase field $Î¸$, for which we derive a bounded phase indicator $P=\tanh(Î²Î¸)$ that provides soft inside--outside cues where they are meaningful. We couple the two fields via a gated-metric formulation with a residual phase injection to obtain a signed implicit function with stable near-surface gradients. The phase coefficient $Î²$ is learnable, allowing MPFs to adaptively control the sharpness of the phase transition and the degree of saturation of the soft sign indicator. Experiments on both synthetic and scanned thin-shell and thin-plate shapes demonstrate that MPFs preserve thin and layered structures more faithfully than recent SDF-based methods, while also enabling more robust training and more reliable surface extraction than UDF-based approaches. Check out \href{https://github.com/JIAYI-Scarlett/ICML2026-MPF}{MPFs-GitHub} for source code and test models.
